_meta.note: PROPOSALS ONLY. tools/agx-isa/db.json was NOT modified. Every match/length change below was applied to a COPY under work/cvar/<name>/ by analysis/make_variant.py and measured by analysis/ab_run.py; the metrics block records the result. The orchestrator owns db.json.

ab_gate.note_on_the_frozen_numbers: The dispatch quotes EXP-0148's endpoint as 832 clean / 389,368 strict leftover bytes. This experiment measures the LIVE tree at 832 clean / 388,872 leftover: the clean-file count is unchanged, and the leftover count has moved by 496 bytes because db.json itself has moved since EXP-0148 (work/DB-DEFECT-TRIAGE.md's (a)/(b) pass landed in between). The gate applied here is therefore no-regression against the LIVE baseline measured in the same run, not against a quoted historical constant.

P1_pixel_order_match.defect: DEF from EXP-0147: the descriptor declares field `flags` at bits[32:40] AND a match constant [32,8,6] pinning those same bits to 0x06, so every legal encoding with byte+4 != 0x06 is neither decodable nor emittable.

prior_attempts_that_FAILED.C1 (drop [32,8,6]): REGRESSES -- the match then equals threadgroup_barrier's and loses the most-specific tie-break (work/DB-DEFECT-TRIAGE.md §4)
prior_attempts_that_FAILED.C1b (byte+1 discriminator): OVER-CLAIMS -- moves 186 real corpus threadgroup_barriers into pixel_order (same source)

change.in_words: drop the byte+4 pin; require instead byte+3 bit4 == 1 AND byte+3 bit6 == 1. byte+4 becomes the genuine field the descriptor already declares.

P1_pixel_order_match.why_this_and_not_the_full_rule: The full hardware-legal byte+3 set is `bit4 AND (bit6 OR bit7)` (union of the two members' measured sets). An OR of two bits is INEXPRESSIBLE in the (start,width,value) match language -- the same blocker as db defects 25 and 50. `bit4 AND bit6` is the largest expressible SUBSET that (a) contains the compiler's own 0x50/0xd0, (b) contains the texture-barrier pair's 0x51/0xd1 that this experiment proved are the same instruction, and (c) contains NO byte+3 value that occurs anywhere in the 1080-file own-MSL corpus. It leaves the bit6==0,bit7==1 half (0x9x/0xbx acquire, 0x9x/0xbx release) still undecodable; that residue is stated, not hidden.

hardware_evidence.detection_power: DETECTION POWER PROVEN, quantitatively: corrupting the acquire member's byte+4 to 0x01 drops the raster-order texel from 8*src to exactly 1*src and the programmable-blend pixel from clear+36*src to clear+8*src, i.e. 7 of 8 serialised read-modify-writes are lost. Reproduced for the release member and for the opcode byte. 22/22 baselines exact.
hardware_evidence.acquire_scope_rule: bit4 == 1 and (bit6 XOR bit7) == 1  [EXACT over the 256 values dispatched; 64 accepted]
hardware_evidence.acquire_flags_rule: (v & 0x01) == 0x00 and (v & 0x0e) != 0  [EXACT over the 256 values dispatched; 112 accepted]
crossform_ordering_PRESERVED: 07 14 54 51 0e 00 at the acquire site  (== threadgroup_barrier(mem_texture) acquire)
07 04 54 d1 0e 00 at the release site  (== threadgroup_barrier(mem_texture) release)
crossform_ordering_LOST: 07 04 54 61 09 00  compute threadgroup_barrier -- 7 of 8 updates lost at BOTH sites
07 04 54 84 0a 00  device mem_fence -- 7 of 8 updates lost at BOTH sites
07 02 54 0c 02 00  fragment tile-ordering barrier -- a DIFFERENT wrong pixel at both sites
hardware_evidence.reading: threadgroup_barrier(mem_texture)'s acquire/release pair IS the pixel_order pair -- proven on hardware, not fitted to a corpus. The three encodings the hardware refuses as raster-order markers are exactly the ones C1b would have stolen, so C1b's failure is now a hardware fact rather than a corpus artifact.

071454500e00.note: acquire with byte+4 = 0x0e (HW ok, undecodable under the old match)

070454d00a00.note: release with byte+4 = 0x0a (HW ok, undecodable under the old match)

070454610900.note: !compute threadgroup_barrier (HW: ordering LOST -- must stay tgbar)

0702540c0200.note: !fragment tile barrier (HW: ordering LOST -- must stay tgbar)

070454840a00.note: !device mem_fence (HW: ordering LOST -- must stay mem_fence)

ab_result.verdict: CLEAN. Corpus metrics byte-identical to baseline, roundtrip ALL PASS, ZERO descriptor firings move. Four encodings the hardware accepts as raster-order markers change from `threadgroup_barrier` (or undecodable-as-pixel_order) to `pixel_order`; the three the hardware REFUSES keep their old mnemonics.

P1_pixel_order_match.residual_unknown: byte+3 values with bit6 == 0 and bit7 == 1 (0x90-0x9f, 0xb0-0xbf) are hardware-legal for both members and remain undecodable under this match. Closing that needs the match language to grow an OR term.
P1_pixel_order_match.also_recommended: relabel the two own-MSL threadgroup_barrier(mem_texture) forms in threadgroup_barrier's semantics: they are this instruction, and this match now decodes them as such.

P2_vary_store_split.class: (c) match AND length change -- alters decoding
P2_vary_store_split.defect: EXP-0091: a byte0==0x57 op in a FRAGMENT main is a 6-byte sample-mask/kill submission op; `vary_store`'s blanket length 8 over-consumes the 2-byte leader of the following instruction and desynchronises the rest of the main. Flagged `emit_unsafe`.
P2_vary_store_split.correction_to_the_dispatch_premise: The dispatch (and db.json's own flag text) identify the fragment op as 'byte0=0x57 with byte+2=0x54'. **byte+2 does NOT discriminate.** In the 1080-file own-MSL corpus byte+2 takes 0x54/0x55/0x56 in BOTH populations (vertex 554/31/40; fragment 4/1/3-and-2), and on hardware byte+2 is FULLY INERT in both forms (256/256 correct on the fragment op, 256/256 on a vertex store).

discriminator.rule: byte+1 bit1: SET = the 8-byte vertex varying store; CLEAR = the 6-byte fragment op
discriminator.corpus: 615/615 vertex tokens set it; 10/10 fragment tokens clear it; zero exceptions
discriminator.second_corpus_correlate: byte+5 separates the corpus equally well (0x40/0x41 vertex vs 0x01 fragment) but is FULLY INERT on hardware in the fragment form (256/256), so it is a corpus correlate, not the hardware selector. byte+1 bit1 is.

hardware_evidence.detection_power: DETECTION POWER PROVEN: splicing the op's byte+4 from 0x00 to 0x01 turns the surviving pixel (0.75,0.5,0.25,1) into the clear colour, and the unspliced mask=0 control does the same -- so the value is live on the rendered-pixel path. 12/12 baselines exact.

fragment_side.0x14 -> 0x16 (bit1 SET, the vertex tag): FRAGMENT KILLED -- the op stops working
fragment_side.0x14 -> 0x1c (bit1 still CLEAR): unchanged, reproducing EXP-0091's M4 null result

vertex_side.byte+1 bit1 CLEARED on a real vary_store: the store's own channel AND downstream channels return garbage floats (e.g. 5.06e32) -- the signature of a stream desync. Reproduced at three different stores.
vertex_side.byte+6 -> 0xFF: NO DRAW at all three stores -- byte+6 is LIVE, so the vertex form is >= 7 bytes
vertex_side.byte+7 -> 0xFF: unchanged at all three stores -- byte+7 inert (matches db's `const 0x00`)

571454000001.note: frag_sample_submit (6 bytes; bytes +6..+7 belong to the NEXT op)

ab_result.verdict: STRICT IMPROVEMENT. roundtrip ALL PASS; clean files 832 -> 833; strict leftover bytes 388,872 -> 388,604 (-268); `frag_sample_submit` fires exactly 10 times and `vary_store` drops by exactly 10, i.e. the split conserves the population; the other deltas are instructions that become reachable once the fragment mains stop desynchronising (+37 tokens net).

P2_vary_store_split.residual_unknown: byte+1 was swept only to 0x5b on the fragment side (2 genuine hangs stopped that byte per FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL section 8), and the vertex-side byte+1/byte+5 sweeps are hang-limited to a few dozen values. The bit1 rule is exact over everything dispatched.

P3_cvt_bf16_match.defect: db defect 26 (deferred in work/DB-DEFECT-TRIAGE.md): the match pins byte+4 == 0x01, but our own compiler emits 0x05, so the compiler's own bfloat convert does not decode as cvt_bf16.
P3_cvt_bf16_match.new_hardware_fact: byte+4 == 0x01 is NOT ACCEPTED BY THE HARDWARE. Dense 0..255 on G17P: 52 of 256 values reproduce the convert and 0x01 is not one of them, while the compiler's 0x05 is. The match constant is not merely narrow, it is WRONG.
P3_cvt_bf16_match.blocked_by: db defect 28: `instr_length()` has NO rule for byte0 == 0x01, so cvt_bf16 cannot be lengthed at all and no match relaxation can reach it. Confirmed again here: the locate pilot tokenizes c_f2bf up to offset 156 and then reports <no-length> on `01 01 14 81 05 02 40 00`. A length rule for byte0 0x01 must land first; that is its own pre-registration.
P3_cvt_bf16_match.not_built_as_a_variant: correct -- it cannot be measured until defect 28 lands
